newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes steady, but ANS offers rise.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes steady, but ANS offers rise.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast light crudes flattened late Monday in line with unchanged values for West Texas Intermediate (WTI). But sellers of Alaskan crude raised their prices following an early sale.
BP America raised its price for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude 20 cents to $1.90 a barrel under December WTI.
The company sold a full cargo of the grade to a major West Coast refinery at a $2.20 discount.
The barrels are slated for December delivery, traders said
The previous ANS spot cargo sold at $2.30 a barrel of October WTI.
Meanwhile, ANS prices remained under pressure from December cash WTI prices, which ended the day 25 cents lower in reaction to profit-taking on the NYMEX.
Line 63 crude also flattened at $20.10/20.40 a barrel.
Wilmington remained at $18.15/$18.25 a barrel, while Kern River crude stayed $16.65/$16.85 a barrel.
